---
title: "Advanced Mathematics for Competitive Programming"
subtitle: "A textbook for expert programmers building mathematical foundations"
---

You already know how to write a fast segment tree, how to squeeze a flow
algorithm under the time limit, and how to debug a tricky DP at two in the
morning. Then a problem says *count the labelled forests modulo $998244353$*,
or *find $x$ with $x^2 \equiv a \pmod p$*, and the difficulty is no longer
engineering. The obstacle is a piece of mathematics that editorials name in
one line and never explain.

This book is the missing explanation. It develops the algebra, number theory,
counting, and probability behind hard ICPC, Codeforces, and AtCoder problems,
starting from definitions and assuming no university mathematics — only that
you are a confident programmer who can follow a careful argument.

Start with [mathematical foundations](00-foundations/chapter.qmd),
then follow the [learning path](STUDY_PLAN.qmd). Keep the
[notation and algebra contracts](NOTATION.qmd) open as a reference.

## What a chapter looks like

Every chapter follows the same rhythm, because that is the order in which
ideas actually become usable:

1. **A problem you cannot yet solve.** Concrete, contest-shaped, and
   deliberately just out of reach.
2. **The object that solves it**, introduced in plain words before any
   notation, with a small example you can check by hand.
3. **Why the central formula is true.** Not a citation — a derivation you
   could reproduce on paper during a contest.
4. **The algorithm's contract:** what it assumes, what it returns, what it
   costs, and the inputs on which it silently returns garbage.
5. **Practice**, from recognizing the model to combining several of them.

The failure modes are not an appendix. Knowing that Fermat inversion breaks
the moment the modulus is composite, or that a formula needs $n < p$ because
it divides by a factorial, is exactly the knowledge that separates a correct
submission from a wrong-answer verdict you cannot explain.

## How to study

Read the derivations with a pen. When a chapter says *why this is true*,
close the page and try to rebuild the argument; the gap you find is the part
you did not actually understand. Work the small numerical examples by hand —
they are chosen so that a misconception produces a visibly wrong number.

Attempt the original exercises before opening their solutions. Use the
external contest problems to practice modelling under uncertainty. Difficulty
labels are relative to this course; they are not predicted contest ratings.
Some exercise pages deliberately point forward to applications that need a
later chapter, and identify those extra prerequisites.

The book assumes you already have a tested competitive-programming library,
so it contains almost no code. It teaches mathematical models, correctness
invariants, input/output contracts, and resource bounds; the implementations
stay in your library. No routine should be selected merely because its name
resembles a phrase in the problem statement.

## Curriculum at a glance {#dependency-map}

Read foundations first, then use these branches. Arrows show the main conceptual
dependencies; the [learning path](STUDY_PLAN.qmd) gives chapter-level details.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  F["Proofs and notation"] --> A["Modular algebra"]
  F --> C["Counting"]
  A --> B["Binomials modulo anything"]
  C --> B
  A --> N["Divisor sums and sieves"]
  A --> L["Linear algebra and recurrences"]
  A --> P["Polynomials and formal series"]
  C --> G["Symmetry and generating functions"]
  P --> G
  C --> T["Subset transforms and set series"]
  L --> R["Probability systems and algebraic graphs"]
  G --> H["Holonomic methods"]
  B --> Q["q-Analogues and subspaces"]
  L --> Q
  N --> X["Mixed and frontier capstones"]
  Q --> X
  R --> X
  T --> X
  H --> X
```

Chapter numbers are the reading order: chapter $n$ relies only on earlier
chapters. Detours are still allowed — the [learning path](STUDY_PLAN.qmd)
lists, for each chapter, the few earlier ones it genuinely uses.

## Chapters

### I · Arithmetic and counting

- [00 · Mathematical foundations and proof](00-foundations/chapter.qmd): notation, logic, induction, invariants, extremal arguments, Bézout, double counting.
- [01 · Modular algebra](01-modular-algebra/chapter.qmd): units, fields, CRT, orders, valuations, logarithms, modular roots.
- [02 · Multiplicative number theory](02-multiplicative-number-theory/chapter.qmd): factorization, arithmetic functions, gcd filters, divisor inversion, Gaussian integers.
- [03 · Combinatorics](03-combinatorics/chapter.qmd) and [practice](03-combinatorics/exercises.qmd): inclusion–exclusion, Stirling and Catalan models, partitions, binomial transforms, rook polynomials.
- [04 · Binomial coefficients modulo anything](04-modular-binomials/chapter.qmd): Lucas, Kummer carries, prime-power factorials, composite moduli by CRT.
- [05 · Group actions](05-group-actions/chapter.qmd) and [practice](05-group-actions/exercises.qmd): orbits, stabilizers, Burnside, Pólya, induced graph symmetries.

### II · Algebraic engines

- [06 · Polynomials](06-polynomials/chapter.qmd) and [practice](06-polynomials/exercises.qmd): convolution, Fourier evaluation, division, product trees, interpolation, Taylor shift.
- [07 · Linear algebra](07-linear-algebra/chapter.qmd): vector spaces, rank, determinants, XOR bases, tree counts, recurrences and black-box methods.
- [08 · Transforms](08-transforms/chapter.qmd): subset and divisor inversion, OR/AND/XOR, ranked disjoint convolution.
- [09 · Formal power series](09-formal-power-series/chapter.qmd) and [practice](09-formal-power-series/exercises.qmd): precision, Newton lifting, inverse, logarithm, exponential, composition and reversion.
- [10 · Generating functions](10-generating-functions/chapter.qmd) and [practice](10-generating-functions/exercises.qmd): labelled and unlabelled models, rational sequences, coefficient extraction, Lagrange inversion.
- [11 · Set power series](11-set-power-series/chapter.qmd): disjoint multiplication, connected components, set exponential and logarithm.

### III · Models and synthesis

- [12 · Probability](12-probability/chapter.qmd): sample spaces, indicators, conditioning, variance, stochastic DP and absorbing systems.
- [13 · Discrete sums and Diophantine tools](13-discrete-sums/chapter.qmd): interpolation, differences, floor sums, rational approximation, Pell equations.
- [14 · Summatory sieves](14-advanced-sieves/chapter.qmd): quotient states, prefix recurrences, prime sums, multiplicative enumeration, powerful support.
- [15 · Mixed capstones](15-capstones/chapter.qmd): modelling workshops with complete reduction guidance.

### IV · Frontier topics

- [16 · q-Analogues and subspace counting](16-q-analogues/chapter.qmd): Gaussian binomials, division-free recurrences, rank distributions.
- [17 · Finite-field polynomials](17-finite-field-polynomials/chapter.qmd): quotient fields, Frobenius, factorization and irreducibility certification.
- [18 · Algebraic graph methods](18-algebraic-graph-methods/chapter.qmd): polynomial identity testing, Pfaffians, Tutte matrices, weighted matching.
- [19 · Holonomic methods](19-holonomic-methods/chapter.qmd): differential equations, polynomial-coefficient recurrences, guessing and certification.
- [20 · Frontier capstones](20-frontier-capstones/chapter.qmd): synthesis with explicit hypotheses, small models and validation plans.

## Formal Power Series & Generating Functions Textbook Track (`Ch 01`–`Ch 24`) {#fps-textbook-track}

Alongside the core 20-chapter mathematics curriculum above, this site hosts the complete **6-Part, 24-Chapter Formal Power Series (FPS) & Generating Functions Textbook** (`Ch 01`–`Ch 24`), paired with **6 Two-Stage Blind Topic-Group Checkpoints** (`CP-I`–`CP-VI`), a **14-Problem Multi-Perspective Synthesis Reserve** (`Syn-01`–`Syn-14`), and a **321-Problem Master Curated Archive** (`254` accepted problems across `192` chapter ladder slots, `48` blind checkpoint slots, and `14` synthesis reserve slots, plus `67` quarantined bare library templates `R-01`–`R-67`).

Every chapter is built from algebraic definitions ($K[[x]]$, $K((x))$, valuation topology $\nu(F)$, formal residues $\operatorname{Res}_{x=0}$, bivariate ring hierarchies, differential Weyl operators $K[x]\langle D \rangle$, Tellegen transposition, Set Power Series $\mathcal{R}_n$, and Dirichlet series $\mathcal{D}_f$) with explicit **Diagnostic Signals**, **Reverse-Engineering Scratchpads**, **Characteristic-$p$ & Valuation-Shift Failure Modes**, and an inline **8-Problem 4-Tier Practice Ladder** (`2 Stepping Stones`, `2 Intermediate`, `2 Advanced`, `2 Mastery`).

### Part I · Foundations of Formal Power Series & Combinatorial Constructions (`Ch 01`–`Ch 04`)

- [FPS Ch 01 · The Ring $K[[x]]$, Valuation Topology & Newton Inversion](chapters/ch01-ring-convolutions-newton-inv.qmd): Cauchy convolution, $x$-adic valuation $\nu(F)$, unit criterion $[x^0]F \in K^\times$, quadratic Newton `inv`, valuation-shift precision loss, and min-heap product trees.
- [FPS Ch 02 · Formal Calculus, 1D Newton Iteration & The $O(NK)$ Sparse Engine](chapters/ch02-calculus-frobenius-sparse-ode-newton.qmd): formal $D_x$ and $\int$, characteristic-$p$ Frobenius endomorphism $A(x)^p \equiv A(x^p) \pmod p$, 1D Newton `sqrt`/`ln`/`exp`/`pow`, 3-way modular reduction in $P(x)^\alpha$, and $O(NK)$ `sparse_div`/`sparse_ln`/`sparse_exp`/`sparse_pow`.
- [FPS Ch 03 · The Unlabeled Symbolic Method: OGFs, Multisets & Partitions](chapters/ch03-mset-partitions-euler-polya.qmd): $\operatorname{SEQ}$, $\operatorname{PSET}$, $\operatorname{MSET}$ (Pólya $\exp$), Inverse Euler Transform via Möbius inversion, Ferrers conjugation, Euler's Pentagonal Number Theorem, and Burnside/Pólya cycle index enumeration.
- [FPS Ch 04 · The Labeled Symbolic Method: EGFs, Boxed Products & Prüfer Trees](chapters/ch04-egf-set-cyc-boxed-prufer.qmd): relabeling binomial convolution, $\operatorname{SET} \mapsto \exp$, $\operatorname{CYC} \mapsto \ln(1-x)^{-1}$, Greene–Wilf Boxed Product $\widehat{C}' = \widehat{A}'\widehat{B}$, Rota's Twelvefold Way, and Prüfer degree-sequence EGFs.
- [FPS Checkpoint I · Part I Blind Assessment (`CP-I`)](checkpoints/cp01-part1-foundations.qmd): 8 two-stage blind diagnostic problems testing `Ch 01`–`Ch 04` recognition without topic tags.

### Part II · Rational Sequences, Binomial Transforms, Roots of Unity & Inclusion–Exclusion (`Ch 05`–`Ch 08`)

- [FPS Ch 05 · Rational Generating Functions $K(x)$, Bostan–Mori & Berlekamp–Massey](chapters/ch05-rational-bostan-mori-berlekamp-massey.qmd): rational series $P(x)/Q(x)$, reversal Euclidean `divmod`, Graeffe parity-splitting Bostan–Mori in $O(d \log d \log N)$, Heaviside partial fractions, and Berlekamp–Massey recurrence synthesis.
- [FPS Ch 06 · Binomial Sums, Snake Oil, Taylor Shift & Stirling Engines](chapters/ch06-binomial-snake-oil-taylor-shift-stirling.qmd): Golden Rule of Index Alignment, Wilf's Snake Oil, Egorychev polynomial negative-exponent extraction, all 4 Stirling row/column $O(N \log N)$ engines, falling-factorial polynomials (`下降幂多项式`), Taylor shift $F(x+c)$, and the generalized $\alpha$-Euler transform.
- [FPS Ch 07 · Point-Value Duality, Roots-of-Unity Filters, Cyclotomic Rings & Chirp-Z](chapters/ch07-roots-of-unity-cyclotomic-czt.qmd): root-of-unity modulo-$m$ filter (`单位根反演`), cyclotomic quotient ring $\mathbb{F}_p[\omega]/(\Phi_m(\omega))$ when $m \nmid (p-1)$, 3-prime Garner NTT (`MTT`), and Bluestein's binomial Chirp Z-Transform $F(ac^i)$.
- [FPS Ch 08 · Sieve & Inclusion–Exclusion Engines: Run-Length Transfer, Rook & Goulden–Jackson](chapters/ch08-connected-component-ie-rook-goulden-jackson.qmd): bivariate Taylor shift $G(x, y-1)$, universal run-length IE $F(x) = W(x)/(1+W(x))$, harmonic sparsity of bounded runs, rook polynomials, and the Goulden–Jackson cluster overlap matrix $\mathbf{C}(x)^{-1}$.
- [FPS Checkpoint II · Part II Blind Assessment (`CP-II`)](checkpoints/cp02-part2-rational-transforms-ie.qmd): 8 two-stage blind diagnostic problems spanning `Ch 01`–`Ch 08`.

### Part III · Online Convolutions, Implicit Equations, Formal Residues & Graph Species (`Ch 09`–`Ch 13`)

- [FPS Ch 09 · Causal Recurrences: CDQ Divide-and-Conquer NTT & Online Relaxed Convolution](chapters/ch09-cdq-fft-online-relaxed-convolution.qmd): semi-online CDQ NTT, full-online self-convolution ($l > 0$ factor-of-$2$ symmetry invariant), van der Hoeven's `lowbit(q+1)` `RelaxedConvolution`, and online Dirichlet updates.
- [FPS Ch 10 · Implicit Functional Equations, Coupled Newton Iteration & Unlabeled Otter Trees](chapters/ch10-implicit-equations-newton-unlabeled-trees-otter.qmd): implicit equations $A(x, F(x)) = 0$, Fréchet derivatives, $2 \times 2$ Jacobian Newton systems, integrating-factor differential Newton, Pólya–Euler rooted trees, and Otter's dissimilarity theorem $U(x) = T(x) - \frac{1}{2}(T(x)^2 - T(x^2))$.
- [FPS Ch 11 · Formal Laurent Series $K((x))$, Residue Calculus, Raney's Lemma & 6-Form LIF](chapters/ch11-laurent-residues-raney-lagrange-inversion.qmd): formal residue invariance $\operatorname{Res}_{x=0} A(x)\,dx = \operatorname{Res}_{u=0} A(G(u))G'(u)\,du$, Raney's cycle lemma and Łukasiewicz paths, all 6 canonical forms of Lagrange Inversion (including char-$p$-safe Derivative-Free LIF), `Elegia` coupled binomial sum linearization, and base-$p$ Frobenius LIF.
- [FPS Ch 12 · Advanced Labeled Graph Species: Pointed Trees, Cacti, Deserts & Tutte Block-Cut Equations](chapters/ch12-cacti-deserts-block-cut-biconnected-graphs.qmd): pointing operator $\Theta = xD_x$, Husimi cacti and deserts, Tutte's pointed block-cut equation $\ln(\widehat{R}(x)/x) = \widehat{B}'(\widehat{R}(x))$, bridge-tree 2-edge-connected graphs, and reverse LIF coefficient extraction.
- [FPS Ch 13 · Graphical Generating Functions: Eulerian, Bipartite, DAGs, SCCs & Symbolic Matrix-Tree](chapters/ch13-graphical-gf-eulerian-bipartite-dags-sccs.qmd): Eulerian and bipartite graph EGFs, Robinson–Stanley layer IE for DAGs and strongly connected digraphs, Wright's fixed-excess kernel decomposition, Kirchhoff Matrix-Tree, BEST theorem, symbolic determinants over $\mathbb{F}_p[x]/(x^{k+1})$, and $O(V^3)$ Hessenberg characteristic polynomials.
- [FPS Checkpoint III · Part III Blind Assessment (`CP-III`)](checkpoints/cp03-part3-online-implicit-lif-graphs.qmd): 8 two-stage blind diagnostic problems spanning `Ch 01`–`Ch 13`.

### Part IV · Stochastic Processes, Lattice Walks, Bivariate Diagonals & The Kernel Method (`Ch 14`–`Ch 17`)

- [FPS Ch 14 · Probability Generating Functions, Stopping Times, Renewal, Poissonization & Martingales](chapters/ch14-pgf-stopping-times-renewal-poisson-martingales.qmd): PGFs $F(z) = \mathbb{E}[z^T]$, formal Taylor shift $z = 1+t \bmod t^3$ for $0/0$ pole cancellation, renewal first-passage deconvolution, KMP border theorem (*The Singing Kingdom*), Poisson–Laplace–Borel bridge, and optional stopping martingales.
- [FPS Ch 15 · 1D Lattice Walks: Reflection Principle, Chebyshev Strips & The Small-Root Kernel Method](chapters/ch15-1d-lattice-walks-chebyshev-kernel-method.qmd): André reflection, Kelvin alternating strip images and Chebyshev polynomials $U_h$, Laurent step ring $(K[y,y^{-1}])[[x]]$, and the 1D Bivariate Kernel Method (single small root, multiple small roots, and Vieta's large-root shortcut).
- [FPS Ch 16 · Multivariate FPS: 5-Ring Hierarchy, 2D Bostan–Mori, Twisted Kronecker & Furstenberg Diagonals](chapters/ch16-bivariate-hierarchy-2d-bostan-mori-furstenberg.qmd): the 5-ring bivariate hierarchy, all 4 regimes of 2D Bostan–Mori (`Truncated`, `Eval-Interp`, `Kinoshita-Li`, `Frobenius`), van der Hoeven's $\chi$-graded twisted Kronecker substitution, Furstenberg's diagonal residue theorem in $K[[t]]((y))$, and Lipshitz 3D D-finite diagonals.
- [FPS Ch 17 · Coupled Multivariate Systems: Quarter-Plane Obstinate Kernel, Good–Lagrange & MacMahon](chapters/ch17-quarter-plane-obstinate-kernel-good-lagrange-macmahon.qmd): Multivariate Good–Lagrange Inversion ($\det(I-J)$ Jacobian and bipartite rank-1 shortcut), MacMahon's Master Theorem $\det(I-XA)^{-1}$, symmetric function ring $\Lambda$ and Newton–Girard char-$p$ asymmetry, 2D quarter-plane Obstinate Kernel Method (dihedral group $\mathcal{G} = \langle \Phi, \Psi \rangle$), and bivariate PDE companion matrix products.
- [FPS Checkpoint IV · Part IV Blind Assessment (`CP-IV`)](checkpoints/cp04-part4-pgf-walks-multivariate.qmd): 8 two-stage blind diagnostic problems spanning `Ch 01`–`Ch 17`.

### Part V · D-Finite Series, Differential Operators, Transposition & Fast Composition (`Ch 18`–`Ch 21`)

- [FPS Ch 18 · D-Finite Series, Euler Operator $\vartheta$, 7 ODE Archetypes & $p$-Adic Indicial Lifting](chapters/ch18-d-finite-weyl-algebra-p-recursive-indicial-lifting.qmd): D-finite $\leftrightarrow$ P-recursive equivalence via $\vartheta = xD_x$, Abel–Cockle–Harley–Comtet algebraic-to-ODE conversion, the 7 ODE linearization archetypes (including Riccati and exponential gauge), and $p$-adic indicial lifting over $\mathbb{Z}/p^{V+1}\mathbb{Z}$.
- [FPS Ch 19 · Shift Algebra, Creative Telescoping (WZ), Coupled Sparse Composition & Truncated Taylor ODEs](chapters/ch19-coupled-sparse-composition-wz-truncated-taylor-ode.qmd): Weyl algebra $K[x]\langle D_x \rangle$ and shift algebra $K[n]\langle E_n \rangle$, Zeilberger WZ pairs, `EI` direct differential-residue binomial sums, coupled $r$-state $O(rNK)$ sparse composition, and `EI 科技` $O(K)$ truncated Taylor ODEs.
- [FPS Ch 20 · Tellegen's Transposition Principle, Middle Product `mulT`, Multipoint Evaluation & Sampling Shift](chapters/ch20-tellegen-transposition-multipoint-sampling-shift.qmd): DAG edge reversal $(E_k \cdots E_1)^\top$, DIF/DIT butterfly duality, middle product `mulT` ($1.5\,\mathcal{M}(N)$ Newton `inv`), division-free transposed multipoint `eval` and `interp`, transposed Chirp-Z ($\text{czt}^\top$), shift of sampling points (`连续点值平移`), and $O(\sqrt{P}\log P)$ block factorials.
- [FPS Ch 21 · Power Projection, Kinoshita–Li $O(N \log^2 N)$ Composition & Dual-Route Compositional Inverse](chapters/ch21-kinoshita-li-composition-power-projection-revert.qmd): `power_projection` via Kinoshita–Li 2D Bostan–Mori ($Q_r(0,y)=1$ zero-inversion invariant), `compose` as the exact Tellegen transpose of `power_projection`, Dual-Route `revert` (Route A for $p > N$, Route B Newton + `compose` for $p \le N$), and functional square roots $G(G(x)) = F(x)$ with the Artin–Schreier obstruction at degree $p+2$.
- [FPS Checkpoint V · Part V Blind Assessment (`CP-V`)](checkpoints/cp05-part5-dfinite-transposition-composition.qmd): 8 two-stage blind diagnostic problems spanning `Ch 01`–`Ch 21`.

### Part VI · Tree-DP Accelerations, $q$-Analogues, Set Power Series & Dirichlet Rings (`Ch 22`–`Ch 24`)

- [FPS Ch 22 · Polynomials on Trees: HLD Spine Divide-and-Conquer, Static Top Trees & Zero-Divisor Maintenance](chapters/ch22-tree-dp-fps-hld-static-top-tree-zero-divisor.qmd): subtree size-convolution bounds, HLD + weight-balanced static top tree (`全局平衡二叉树`) with min-heap `Rake` and 3-way weighted-midpoint `Compress`, Fourier-domain $3c^2$ matrix products, zero-divisor pairs $(a,c) \equiv a\cdot 0^c$, and rerooting Vandermonde `mulT`.
- [FPS Ch 23 · $q$-Analogues, Gaussian Binomials, $q$-Difference Equations, $q$-Lucas & MacWilliams Duality](chapters/ch23-q-analogues-gaussian-binomials-q-lucas-macwilliams.qmd): $q$-Pochhammer $(a;q)_n$, Gaussian $q$-binomials $\binom{n}{k}_q$, Gauss/Cauchy $q$-binomial theorems, $q$-difference equations ($x \mapsto qx$), $q$-Lucas theorem when $\operatorname{ord}_p(q) \le n$, Durfee squares, Grassmannian subspace counting over $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, and MacWilliams/Krawtchouk coding duality.
- [FPS Ch 24 · Non-Cauchy Algebras: Bitwise FWT, Set Power Series $\mathcal{R}_n$ & Dirichlet Ring $\mathcal{D}_f$](chapters/ch24-bitwise-fwt-set-power-series-dirichlet_gf.qmd): OR/AND/XOR FWT, Set Power Series $\mathcal{R}_n = K[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(x_1^2,\dots,x_n^2)$, L1-contiguous ranked FZT, division-free $O(n^2 2^n)$ SPS `inv`/`ln`/`exp` via MSB derivative $\partial/\partial x_v$, `Elegia` Taylor-shift SPS composition, pointed biconnected SPS $\ln$, and Dirichlet series $\mathcal{D}_f$ with prime-multiplicity $\Omega(n)$-derivation $\vartheta$.
- [FPS Checkpoint VI · Part VI Blind Assessment (`CP-VI`)](checkpoints/cp06-part6-trees-qseries-sps-dirichlet.qmd): 8 two-stage blind diagnostic problems spanning the entire 24-chapter FPS curriculum.

## What mastery means

For each chapter, record whether you can define its objects, reproduce its
central proof, solve its local exercises, recognize its model in a contest
statement, and explain a counterexample to its misuse. Revisit a difficult
problem after two and six weeks; successful recall of the derivation is more
informative than recognizing an editorial.

The course concentrates on algebra, number theory, counting, and probability.
Geometry and continuous optimization are outside this curriculum. No finite
toolkit covers every future contest problem; the transferable skill is deriving
a new variant from well-understood objects and assumptions.

See the [source and verification policy](SOURCES.qmd) for reference standards.
